svg.text: THE FACADE + THE ONE BIG SEAM
one wide interface — a real system would split it into 4 (identity, graph, content, feed)
chronological today; engagement- or ML-ranked later, same signature
honest: notifyPostLike and notifyComment are EMPTY stubs today
THE CORE — six registries + two injected policies
posts: CHM<String, Post> · comments: CHM<String, Comment>
sendFriendRequest — rejects self, blocked, duplicate, already-friends
→ only the RECEIVER may accept or reject (UnauthorizedException)
acceptFriendRequest — writes BOTH sides of the friendship
blockUser — also tears down the existing friendship
isVisibleToUser(post, viewer) — block wins over visibility
getNewsfeed — filter by visibility, then delegate to feedAlgorithm
blocking is enforced, not merely stored — storing it without consulting it
makes the feature decorative, and that is a SAFETY bug ✓
conversations use CopyOnWriteArrayList — a plain ArrayList inside a CHM
sendFriendRequest's duplicate check STREAMS every request — O(all requests),
and it is check-then-act: two concurrent sends can both create one
no index of posts-by-author, so getNewsfeed scans EVERY post in the system
searchUsers / searchPosts are O(n) toLowerCase scans
the registries are concurrent; the collections INSIDE User and Post are not —
plain HashSet / ArrayList. That is the honest concurrency ceiling here.
CHM = ConcurrentHashMap · ids are UUIDs, no typed-id value objects
THE MODEL — the graph lives on the User
friendIds: Set<String> ← MUTUAL, both sides written
blockedUserIds: Set<String> ← consulted on EVERY interaction
every getter returns a defensive copy (new HashSet<>)
friend = mutual accept · follow = one-sided, no consent ✓
the sets are plain HashSets — not safe under concurrent writes
likeUserIds: Set<String> ← a SET, so likes are idempotent
likeUserIds is a Set ⇒ double-liking is a no-op, not a double count ✓
sharePost copies the TEXT, it does not reference the original —
so an edit to the original never propagates to the share
both terminal — requirePending() makes a second answer throw ✓
accept() then writes friendIds on BOTH users — mutual by construction
conversationId = sorted(a,b) ⇒ one thread per pair ✓
only FRIEND_REQUEST and USER_FOLLOWED are actually emitted;
notifyPostLike / notifyComment are empty method bodies today
the extension point exists; the subscribers do not — say that, don't hide it
① SocialNetwork facade → service seam → ② the six registries → ③ User's four sets (friend vs follow vs block) → FriendRequest's state machine → then FeedAlgorithm as the Strategy knob

g.text: THE AUTHORIZATION BUG WORTH NAMING — acceptFriendRequest(requestId) with no actor
Without an accepterId parameter, the SENDER can accept their own request and befriend anyone unilaterally. The whole point of a
friend request is mutual consent, so the signature must carry the actor: acceptFriendRequest(requestId, accepterId).
requireRequestFor() then checks request.getReceiverId().equals(responderId) and throws UnauthorizedException otherwise.
Same shape as the blocking bug: an authorization field that is stored but never consulted is not a feature, it is a false promise.
THE FEED SCALE ANSWER (the follow-up you WILL get)
Today: getNewsfeed streams EVERY post, filters by visibility, then ranks. That is pull-on-read,
O(all posts) per call. Fine for a demo, hopeless at scale.
Real answer: fan-out-on-write into a per-user feed store, EXCEPT for celebrities
(millions of followers) — those stay pull-on-read and get merged in. The hybrid is the expected answer.

Patterns: Facade · Strategy (FeedAlgorithm) · Observer-ish (NotificationService) · tiny State (FriendRequest) · canonical pair key (conversations)
Honest gaps: model collections are not concurrent · no posts-by-author index · O(n) search · duplicate-request check is a scan AND check-then-act
